analysis.name: Amber Bryant
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 85 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Her class is not difficult in the slightest, with quizzes and exams being open-note.

Assignments are straightforward. 

She has a midterm which covers the first textbook and a final that covers the second; her final is not cumulative.

Unfortunately, her lectures are not all that interesting. I often found myself confused in certain sections.

This class is so easy. One assignment a week. Attendance is mandatory but it's only worth five points of your overall grade so you're fine if you don't go. Exams and quizzes use lockdown browser but she moved every one to taking it remote so it didn't matter. Easy ISS to 4.0.

She's such a sweetheart! During her first lecture, she said something under the lines of wanting all of us to get A's (which she said was 100% possible) and she hoped to be able to interact with all of us. Her feedback to our online papers/responses shows she cares about our performance, and her lectures are easy to navigate.

Dr. Bryant has been my favorite professor at MSU so far. I took her class to meet a school requirement but found myself actually interested in her lectures and the material. The textbook is free and though attendance is mandatory, she is very understanding. She wants you to do well!

Super nice professor who cares about the material she's teaching and cares about students. Very straight forward and easy class. Every quiz question was bar for bar from the combined lecture notes SHE would provide and let you print and take to the quiz. Not possible to fail. Also canceled class or finished early many times. 10/10

analysis.name: Jeff Ackermann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 115 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: With little to no choice for an economics class, you will most likely get stuck with Ackermann. If this happens, I hope you are good at teaching yourself the entirety of microeconomics. Even with the video lectures, much is up to interpretation during the exams when you have to study eight different units for a single exam. Would not take again.

Honestly it's a whatever class, I can't claim bias or anything, but like I showed up, 3rd row to front, quiet, attentively. But its like every interaction is lol why do you like hate me. Like I just take it personal sometimes and couldn't help but feel like rip me. Like idk I think he's rude and bald sorry.

Wrong answers on practice assignments. Conflicting info between textbook/Connect/lectures. Connect hw was torture, sometimes you'd answer 100+ questions (2 hrs) for one chapter. Then go do his hw assignment & realize it's different. Tanked the final despite studying for 6 hrs for it bc the wording was confusing (also he was really noisy during it?)

His class wasn't difficult per se. However, Professor Ackermann fought my RCPD coordinator on midterm extensions. I had life saving surgery, and only received a two-day extension for the first midterm. The work is definitely manageable, but his schedule is incredibly strict. Also, in-person exams for an online course are brutal. (EC 201 & 202)

Ackerman is a really nice guy and you can tell he loves the subject but he is not a good professor. He explains things in a very confusing way and the way that homework assignments and exams are written are just bad. My dad is also an econ professor and even he said that the questions made no sense. I'd recommend going to tutoring outside of class.

Super sweet and caring and available outside of class to discuss grades. Attendance was not mandatory either. Take her for PSY 101!
Very chill class, exams match the lecture notes!
Great professor. Easy class if you go to lecture and use the study guides. Pay attention to the times that things are due though. Will screw you over
Amazing professor! She is very sweet. Tons of extra credit opportunities and the study guides are very close to the exams which she makes pretty straightforward.

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely worst professor I have had in class. There are three exams and like five random in person assignments that happen at the end of the year. The exams are entirely based on lectures which he does not post. He is absolutely no help outside of the classroom. Exams are extremely difficult even if you attend every lecture. Would not reccomend.

For a class that has 75% of the final grade dedicated to your exam performance, you'd think there would be more material to actually practice for it.
The professor himself is nice, but asks WAY too much of his students.
(Depending on your major or minor, you could substitute something like STT 200 [much easier] for this class - ask your advisor.)

Ron is a great guy. He's funny, he's engaging in his lectures, and is clearly passionate about his teaching career. However, his exam's are near impossible. The answers are so incredibly similar that it will make your head spin, yes physically spin. The exams are worth 75% of your grade so each one feels like stepping onto a battlefield. Good luck.

Ron is a great guy but probably the worst teacher I have ever had. You could know the material and study a lot and still not know the answers to the exams. In a class where exams are 75% of the grade he as a teacher seems to take pride in making his exams hard and his questions confusingly worded with multiple correct answers. Take someone else!

My fav professor by FAR. sweetest man you will ever meet and an amazing, clear, professor. I have 0 clue why he has any bad reviews. the class has 0 hw, and the exams are not that hard as long as you study a quizlet and look at the study guide. entertaining lectures and does not take attendance, yet somehow everyone shows up. LOVES his wife,10/10.

Professor Stanton gave great feedback, cared about how her students did, and was not a harsh grader. I would definitely recommend taking this course.

Don't be discouraged from her class. She's attentive and engages, so anticipate her walking around n asking questions. Workload is manageable. She goes out her way to help best she can. Stay after class if u have questions; she addresses them transparently and guides u step by step. There's a textbook & subscription, but u can pass w/o if u engage.

analysis.name: Eric Aronoff
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Aronoff is one of the best English teachers I've ever had, and I mean that very genuinely. I think I say this mainly because of the way that he grades papers. There's a lot of them, sure, they're a bulk of the class. But he gives genuine feedback, and it's very obvious that he wants you to improve and dig deeper into the text. Great guy.

Reading was the main downside of this class, yet Aronoff made it significantly more fun. Brought doughnuts for students on days where lengthy reading or projects were due. Gives amazing feedback and is always willing to work with students to rewrite papers or improve their grade

Great professor who is super passionate about what he is teaching. He makes sure you engage in class and genuinely will listen to what you have to say. He gives really good feedback on essays and will meet one on one with you to discuss your writing. Overall a great class!
Great professor, highly involved in his students' work. Loves what he teaches, and it's so infectious, you will too.

review_highlights.comment: This professor has the ability to simplify complex topics so students can understand and truly cares about the success of students. The practice problems and quizzes matched perfectly with the exams, and there were never any surprises. I took this class accelerated in 6 weeks instead of 16 and it was an easy 4.0.

Take Ayoob for orgo, and nobody else. his 8am lectures both semesters are the only 8am classes I've ever taken, only because I actually loved the class. Orgo is notoriously a weeder class but NOT Ayoobs class. You will learn the material so well and enjoy it. This might be a hot take but general chem was harder than his classes. Take his class!

He is a great teacher, cares about his students' learning. Organic chemistry is difficult, but he makes it manageable. It's very possible to get a 4.0, which is great for this class. He offers lots of extra credit, so even exam averages in the 60s can still earn a 4.0. Homework is easy with multiple attempts, and the 4 quizzes can be retaken.

Bazgir made the class way too easy with the amount of extra credit he handed out. But it's hard to learn from him since he just gives the answers to everything rather than actually teaching. Also skipped spectroscopy completely last semester (just emailed everyone and said "study it on your own").

He makes chemistry so easy with his comparisons to real-world analysis. He truly wants all his students to see how complex concepts can be broken down in simple ways. He allows students to engage during lectures free of shame. He makes funny jokes and does call-and-responses so we all stay engaged. 10% EC boost to your grade. Everyone loves him

Just take it somewhere else I would not recommend! 4 years of college and this is one of the weirdest experiences with an online class. Hopefully MSU does something about him.

The class is super interesting but be prepared to get a bad grade even if you do the work and pay attention. The exam questions are meant to be trick questions he is literally out to get you

Is water wet? (choose one)

-Yes, but no

Professor Bennett is a nice guy but has a weirdly big ego, which seems to be a trend among young philosophy professors.

I'm a bit confused by some of the reviews here. I didn't read any of the books aside from light skimming here and there, and received a 4.0 in the course. Papers weren't graded too harshly, and the final was very easy.
Lectures can certainly be a bit boring, but the slides summed up everything I needed for papers and the exam.
